Medicare Advantage, non-contracted: each reconsideration either pays or goes to the CMS independent review entity on its own after 60 days (422.590(b)(2), (d)); for ALJ hearings, claims for similar or related services can be aggregated to meet the amount in controversy (42 CFR 405.1006(e), per the medicare_advantage area).

Commercial group plans: pull the payer's monthly Transparency in Coverage in-network rate file for the practice's NPI and TIN to price every line (29 CFR 2590.715-2715A3); this proves underpayments at scale without opening contracts.

Regulators as a batch channel: one complaint per payer per pattern with counts, dates and dollars. Kentucky insurers answer the Department in 15 days (KRS 304.2-165); Indiana insurers give a written report with specific reasons in 20 business days (IC 27-4-1-5.6(d)); CMS requires MA plans to resolve tracked complaints in 30 days (42 CFR 422.125).

Pattern evidence has legal weight: it defeats the de minimis excuse for ERISA and ACA procedural failures (2590.715-2719(b)(2)(ii)(F)(2)), meets Indiana's 'general practice' standard (IC 27-4-1-4(a)(16)) and Kentucky's 'pattern of repeated violations' fine (KRS 304.99-123(1)(b)). Aggregate defects per payer automatically.

Fax as the channel: lawful for payment disputes (45 CFR 164.506(c)(1)), but minimum necessary applies (164.502(b)) and a misdirected fax is presumed a breach (164.402); take fax numbers only from current payer manuals and keep transmission confirmations, which some rules use as the filing date. TCPA junk-fax rules do not apply to non-advertising disputes (47 U.S.C. 227(a)(5)).

Small claims is not a scale channel in Kentucky: $2,500 cap, 25 filings a year per location, no assigned claims (KRS 24A.230, 24A.240, 24A.250). Use it selectively where fee shifting applies (KRS 304.12-235(3)).
Human review in the loop: Indiana requires a person to review any claim an automated tool submits (IC 27-1-52-9(b)); keep one-click human approval on every corrected claim and every appeal batch.
does_not_apply: State prompt pay, unfair claims, utilization review and external review statutes (KRS 304.17A, 304.12-230; IC 27-8-5.7, 27-4-1, 27-1-37.5, 27-1-52) do not govern Medicare Advantage plans: 42 CFR 422.402 supersedes state law other than licensing and solvency, and Barrows v. Humana (W.D. Ky. 2025) dismissed state statutory unfair-claims and bad-faith claims against Humana MA as preempted.

Self-funded ERISA plans (UMR, UHC Shared Services and other administrative-services-only plans, many Anthem and Cigna employer groups) are outside state insurance law; federal ERISA and ACA claims rules, the plan documents and the provider contract govern. Kentucky's own definition of insurer excludes self-insurers exempt under ERISA (per kentucky area).
Indiana's downcoding chapter (IC 27-1-52) excludes the Medicaid program and Medicaid MCOs (27-1-52-0.3).

Medicare Advantage Subpart M appeals and independent review do not apply to contracted-provider payment disputes when the enrollee owes nothing more (42 CFR 422.562(c)(2)); the contract's dispute and arbitration terms apply.
The TCPA junk-fax ban (47 U.S.C. 227(b)(1)(C)) does not apply to appeals, disputes or complaints, which are not advertisements.

No statute was found in Kentucky or Indiana that protects a provider from network termination without cause for filing appeals or complaints; only anti-gag provisions (KRS 304.17A-530; IC 27-8-11-4.5; IC 27-13-15-1) and narrow federal rules (42 CFR 422.570(f), 422.584(f), 438.410(b)) exist.
The statutory limits on Medicare nonrandom prepayment review (former 42 U.S.C. 1395kk-1(h)) were repealed in 2010.
Kentucky small claims bars assigned claims (KRS 24A.240(2)), so a provider suing as a patient's assignee cannot use it.

The algorithmic-denial class actions (Lokken, Barrows, Kisting-Leung) are member cases; providers are not parties, the rulings are district-court decisions without binding force elsewhere, and none creates a provider cause of action.
The CMS Feb. 6, 2024 FAQ is guidance interpreting 42 CFR 422.101(c), not a regulation; cite it with the regulation.
806 KAR 12:092 says it exists to guide the commissioner (Section 2(2)); it is not itself a private right of action.
No Surprises Act IDR (45 CFR 149.510) applies only to qualified out-of-network items; in-network office dermatology rate disputes do not qualify.
